title: Position and ordering blind spots shared across models: a correlated-bias incident study

original_idea.body:
# Position and ordering blind spots shared across models

Permute answer positions/order across models on MCQ and pairwise-preference sets; measure each model's bias and test cross-model correlation. Estimate the fraction of items where one reorder flips ALL models. Public benchmarks + inference.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Level 3: plausible chain (shared position bias = single-manipulation fleet exploit) but catastrophic link is generic.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Level 5: permute positions, measure bias, test correlation on public sets; beginner-accessible.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Level 5: tightly scoped single experiment (correlated bias + flip fraction) with clear metrics.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Level 4: public benchmarks + inference, weak lab incentive, no internal access.

low_compute.reasoning: Inference on public benchmarks, minimal compute.

novelty.reasoning: Position bias documented; cross-model correlation as a shared exploit may be open.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Position/order biases known; the cross-vendor correlated-flip angle is plausibly underexplored.
